properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. The most interesting idea in the batch and the least evidenced. Nothing here is settled.

THE CRATE: dynograph-game is not even a dependency of reflow2 today. It is closed-form normal-form analysis — per-player dominant strategies, pure Nash equilibria, Pareto-optimal outcomes, the interior 2x2 mixed equilibrium, and a headline classification `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` with the Pareto outcome that dominates each suboptimal equilibrium.

THE FIT, and it is to a context Anthony has stated rather than one invented here: his real operating environment is several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs — A wants X, B wants Y, C built its own because it could not wait — and the job is making them interoperate when they were never designed to. That is a normal-form game. Players are organisations. Strategies are {adopt the shared interface, build our own}. And `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` is exactly the interoperability tragedy: every organisation behaves rationally, every one builds its own, and the system of systems is collectively worse. The crate names both the equilibrium and the outcome that dominates it.

ADJACENT: dec:mosa-conformance is open, and MOSA is fundamentally an argument about the incentives to use open interfaces rather than about the interfaces themselves.

THE CONFLICT TO BE CLEAR ABOUT: the OBVIOUS application is analysis of alternatives — score the options, compute the equilibrium. That would CONTRADICT dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable, which is accepted and says "alternatives are unranked forkable siblings; the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score". Computing an equilibrium over design alternatives IS a stored recommendation. This must not be done without reopening that decision explicitly (dec:reopen-supersedes gives the mechanism). The interoperability reading does NOT conflict, because reflow2 would be reporting a structural property of an incentive situation a human described, not preferring a design — the same posture as dec:report-dont-judge.

THE HARD COST: payoffs are not in the graph and cannot be invented. This needs new vocabulary (players, strategies, payoff matrix) and a capture path, so it is M-to-L, not a spike. It is a product question about what reflow2 is for, and wants a conversation and a Decision before any code.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 model multi-organisation interoperability as a normal-form game?
properties.rationale: Recorded because the fit to the stated multi-organisation context is unusually good, and recorded WITH the conflict against dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable stated in the same node, so nobody can pick this up later without meeting the objection.
